technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the Lattice 0.6.0 upgrade as a compatibility change across application code, build files, tests, documentation, and UI assets rather than only changing a version string.

Perform Spring XD to Spring Cloud Data Flow replacements consistently in source code, user-visible text, documentation, configuration examples, tests, and scripts, while preserving compatibility with third-party API names where required.
Replace Job and Jobs terminology with Task and Tasks in user-facing and product-owned code, while retaining external library identifiers when changing them would break the underlying API.
Use a shared visual style for admin-ui and Flo, including typography, color palette, spacing, navigation treatment, buttons, forms, and common branding components.
Expose the admin-ui version from build or package metadata and expose the SPI type from the active runtime configuration, with graceful fallback text when either value is unavailable.
Add Flo Graph screenshots to the batch DSL documentation using a reproducible capture process and stable image assets stored with the documentation.
Implement scale-up and scale-down as direct Data Flow shell commands that delegate to the existing server/module scaling operation, rather than exposing SPI-specific commands directly to users.
Validate scale commands with argument validation, clear error messages, and compatibility with the supported deployment SPI implementations.
Use automated unit and integration tests for behavior changes, supplemented by manual UI, documentation, CLI, and cross-component acceptance checks.
assumptions: The existing Lattice repository, admin-ui, Flo, shell, documentation, and build infrastructure are available and can be modified by one developer.
Lattice 0.6.0 dependencies and migration notes are available, and the upgrade does not require a major redesign of the application architecture.
The increment targets Java 17 or a compatible runtime where required by the selected Spring Framework version.
The existing project has established build, test, and packaging conventions that can be reused.

The required scale operation is already supported by the Data Flow server and relevant SPI implementations; this increment adds the direct shell abstraction rather than implementing new infrastructure scaling mechanisms.

The scope of terminology replacement includes product-owned source, tests, UI labels, documentation, examples, and scripts, but not immutable third-party package names or historical migration references where those must remain accurate.
No new authentication, authorization model, deployment platform, or persistence schema is required.
Existing visual assets and Flo rendering capabilities are sufficient to produce the requested screenshots without developing a new graph renderer.
A workday represents one developer day of focused effort, including coding, review of one's own changes, testing, and documentation; elapsed calendar duration and parallel staffing are not estimated.
The estimate includes normal local debugging and regression correction but excludes major redesign discovered during the design-gap review.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the repository structure, dependency graph, build profiles, existing UI and Flo implementations, shell commands, documentation, tests, and all locations affected by the eight user stories. Produce an implementation checklist and identify upgrade risks.

Update Lattice dependencies and related configuration, resolve source and API incompatibilities, adjust build and packaging configuration, and update affected tests and examples so the project builds against release 0.6.0.

activities.activity_name: Spring Cloud Data Flow terminology migration
activities.activity_description: Replace Spring XD references with Spring Cloud Data Flow throughout product-owned source code, UI text, tests, documentation, scripts, configuration examples, and generated or displayed metadata, while preserving required external identifiers.

Replace product-owned Job and Jobs terminology with Task and Tasks across APIs exposed by the product, UI labels, command help, documentation, examples, tests, and validation messages, with compatibility handling for unavoidable external names.

Review the existing styling and interaction patterns, define shared visual tokens and conventions, update admin-ui and Flo components, and verify consistent branding, layout, typography, controls, navigation, and responsive behavior.
Add version and SPI type retrieval and presentation to the admin-ui About section, including build metadata wiring, runtime configuration access, fallback behavior, formatting, and UI tests.

Create representative Flo Graphs for the batch DSL concepts, capture and optimize screenshots, integrate the images into the relevant documentation, add explanatory captions or references, and verify the documentation rendering.

Revisit the current design, inspect known limitations and missing capabilities, compare behavior across supported components and SPIs, document identified gaps and risks, and record recommendations or explicit out-of-scope items.

Design and implement user-facing shell commands for scaling a selected module instance up or down, including command syntax, option parsing, validation, server interaction, SPI-independent delegation, output, and error handling.

Add or update unit, component, shell, UI, and integration tests for the dependency upgrade, terminology changes, About metadata, visual-facing behavior, and scale commands, including success and failure cases.

activities.activity_name: Build, CI, packaging, and documentation validation
activities.activity_description: Run and repair the complete build and test pipeline, validate generated artifacts and metadata, check documentation links and image packaging, and confirm that CI and release-oriented checks remain compatible with the upgraded dependencies.

Perform manual acceptance checks across admin-ui, Flo, documentation, and shell workflows; verify representative module scaling and metadata display; investigate regressions; and apply final corrective changes.
